title: Gas Venting Improvements: PVC Gas-Vent Rating, Fittings, and Safety (This Old House)

summary: This Old House presenter explains how venting of gas appliances evolved from galvanized smoke pipe venting up a chimney to newer practices that vent exhaust horizontally to the outdoors. He explains that higher appliance efficiency lowers flue gas temperature and lift, which made galvanized pipe unsuitable, prompting a shift to venting materials like PVC; however, plain drain-waste-vent PVC is not rated for venting hot gases and can suffer thermal aging, discoloration, brittleness, and even leaks that release carbon monoxide. The standard now requires gas-vent rated PVC, with both pipe and fittings from the same manufacturer to ensure airtight joints. Visible signs of failure (discoloration or brittle, expanding/contracting sections) warrant professional inspection, and a working CO detector is advised as inexpensive safety insurance.
